elements.element: Customer is subject to no non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 states that Customer has made no non-compete commitment and broadly permits Customer to develop, acquire, license, sell, or use any product or service. Section 12.4 affirmatively permits activities involving products or services that compete with Vendor.

elements.element: Customer is subject to no field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited to a named competing product.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains, so the condition for limiting a restriction to a named competing product is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains during or after the term.

elements.element: Any restriction is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains, so no restricted period exceeds 12 months.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Sections 12.3 and 12.4 affirmatively permit Customer to develop any product or service, including competing products, without limiting that permission to external development.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for acquisitions by Customer.
elements.evidence: Sections 12.3 and 12.4 expressly permit Customer to acquire any product or service, including one that competes with Vendor.

result.reason: The operative language fully removes both non-compete and field-of-use restrictions, satisfying the preferred position and necessarily remaining within every fallback limit. It preserves unrelated terms and resolves the prior contradiction. It is not strictly minimal because deleting former Section 12.4 would have sufficed; the new affirmative permission largely duplicates Section 12.3.
